hero.oneLiner: The deck positions HomeFirst as a technology-driven affordable housing finance company with pan-India, hub-and-spoke distribution, lending to first-time home buyers (predominantly families earning under Rs 50,000 p.m.) on the back of data-science-backed centralised underwriting and a diversified AA-rated funding franchise.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "Technology driven affordable housing finance company with pan India presence. Hub and spoke distribution covering 80% of the affordable housing market in the country."
- "Home loans to first time home buyers with predominant focus on families with a monthly income of < Rs 50,000 p.m. 83% of AUM comprises housing loans with an average ticket size of Rs 1.21 Mn."
- "Data science backed centralized underwriting integrated with Account Aggregator. Proprietary customer scoring models supported by digital data sources." 85% of loans approved within 48hrs; 100+ data points digitally captured for all customers, with API integration to third-party sources like Hunter and Perfios.
- Value proposition targets customers who face documentation barriers at traditional lenders: loans are right-sized through holistic evaluation of formal/informal income and alternative documents (life insurance policies, property deeds), with 48 Hr turn-around for approval and no prepayment charges. NPS for Q1FY27 is 79.
- "Strong culture of continuous learning, innovation and improvement in productivity. Young, empowered employees with a customer centric mindset. 1,988 employees with a median age of 26 years."

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)
capital_allocation.body:
- Capitalisation is well above requirement and has been rebuilt by equity issuance: CRAR 42.6% at Q1FY27 (Tier I 42.2%) vs 32.8% in FY25; the journey slide notes "Raised ₹1,250 Cr through QIP", and net worth stands at ₹44,827 Mn at Jun'26 vs ₹25,213 Mn at Mar'25.
- Leverage is deliberately low: Leverage (average total assets / average net worth) of 3.5x in Q1FY27 vs 4.7x in FY25; average debt to equity ratio 2.4 in Q1FY27 vs 3.6 in FY25.
- Liability strategy: 32 lending partners, long-term rating of AA 'Stable' from ICRA, CARE and India Ratings, short-term A1+ (ICRA and India Ratings), and "ZERO borrowing through commercial papers". NHB is the single largest lender with ₹19,601.4 Mn outstanding.
- Liquidity buffer as on Jun'26 of ₹22,724 Mn (unencumbered cash and cash equivalent ₹11,434 Mn, un-availed sanction from NHB ₹3,540 Mn, un-availed sanction from banks ₹7,750 Mn); liquidity raised during Q1FY27 of ₹5,814 million; ALM shows cumulative positive flows across all time buckets.
- Employee ownership is an explicit allocation choice: total ESOPs in force as % of total paid-up capital at Jun'26 is 3.6% (Mar'26: 3.0%), with 300 employees covered under ESOP programs, comprising 15.1% of the employee base, and 4 ESOP plans implemented. The deck does not mention a dividend.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Management change] The CFO slide carries the note "Nutan Gaba Patwari has resigned. We thank her for her valuable contribution to the organization."
- [Board change] Divya Sehgal (Nominee / Non-Executive Director, Partner at True North) "Ceased to be director w.e.f. Jun 24, 2026".
- [Shareholding] As on 17 Jul'26 the register is institution-dominated: FIIs & FPIs 48.4%, DIIs 36.0%, Public & Others 15.6%, across 81,777 shareholders. Largest single holders disclosed are Fidelity International 9.6%, HDFC Mutual Fund 7.6%, Capital Group 7.1%, Norges Bank Investment Management 5.3% and Kotak Mutual Fund 5.1%.
- [PMAY] "Throughout the duration of PMAY programme, a total of 38,507 customers were assisted with the PMAY subsidy benefit from NHB, amounting to cumulative credit of Rs. 966.4 Cr to their account. This has helped reduce ~26% of Loan Amount for those customers"; 698 customers have already benefitted under PMAY (U) 2.0.
- [Clean record] Governance slide claims: "NO Defaults. NO Auditor qualification. NO Re-statements of financials. NO Allegations of financial imprudence."
